Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The NIS is interfaced with multiple government systems providing online authentication of person identity and data. Government agencies query the NIS for authentication. The system supports real-time online authentication for services including electoral system, SOBERS, payroll and transport. A new fully digital authentication system is planned for the Digital ID rollout.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Government portals use Omang for authentication. The DRTS (Department of Road Transport Services) e-services portal requires Omang/Passport number for login. The 1Gov1Citizen platform being rolled out allows citizens to access government services online. The new Digital ID system is designed to interface with all national digital platform services.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No self-service portal exists for individuals to view their own NIS data. Section 20 of the National Registration Act restricts public access to the registry. While the 2024 Data Protection Act grants data subjects the right to access personal data held by controllers, this has not yet translated into a citizen-facing portal for the NIS. The planned Digital ID system envisages citizens being able to view their records.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Bank of Botswana banking regulations explicitly require Omang for KYC/customer identification. Financial institutions must verify identity using Omang for citizens. SIM card KYC requires Omang. The new Digital ID system explicitly aims to support electronic KYC (eKYC) with digital signatures and automated data exchange.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Botswana established a full organic link between birth registration, national registration (Omang), and death registration through a single unique identifier in 2003. The NIS is updated in real time when deaths are registered. UNICEF describes the two systems (CRVS and NIS) as 'operating efficiently and mutually interoperable'.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Section 20 of the National Registration Act restricts disclosure; Minister authorizes specific departments via schedule. Data is shared with government agencies (electoral, SOBERS, payroll, transport) via MoU on a yes/no query basis. The 2024 Data Protection Act adds specific data sharing and cross-border data transfer rules. Full data transfer is prohibited without authorization.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No specific digital ID regulation exists. The system is governed by the National Registration Act which predates digital systems. The new Digital ID/Electronic ID system being developed (pilot 2025, rollout 2026) has not yet produced specific digital ID legislation. The National Registration (Amendment) Act of 2025 updated some provisions.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Botswana enacted the Data Protection Act in 2018 (though not fully operationalized initially). A new, comprehensive Data Protection Act was enacted in 2024, aligning more closely with GDPR. It establishes the Information and Data Protection Commission, mandates DPIAs, requires breach notification within 72 hours, and introduces Data Protection Officers.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Information and Data Protection Commission is designated as the national supervisory authority under both the 2018 and 2024 Data Protection Acts. It monitors and enforces the Act, promotes awareness, handles complaints, and conducts investigations. The 2024 Act strengthened its independence and operational structure.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The Omang card is designated as prima facie proof of identity under the National Registration Act. It serves as the primary document for accessing public services, voter registration, passport application, driving license, and other legal purposes.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: The National Registration Act CAP 01:02 provides the legal basis for compulsory national registration. The Births and Deaths Registration Act covers CRVS. The Electronic Transactions Act governs digital signatures. These create a comprehensive legal framework for the identity system.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The DCNR is under the Ministry of Labour and Home Affairs (MLHA), not the Ministry of Finance. However, the Ministry of Finance provides general PFM oversight through budget approvals and the Public Finance Management framework. Annual ID system budgets are allocated through parliament. The MLHA has its own budget approved by parliament including P105 million for Omang card production in 2026/27.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The Botswana ID system is primarily funded from domestic budget. Annual operating budget is approximately US$5.6 million (2014/15), with additional P105 million (approx US$7.7 million) for Omang card production in 2026/27. While international partners (UNICEF, World Bank) provided some technical assistance, core financing is domestic through the national development plans.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Botswana collects fingerprints (two thumbprints) and facial photo at enrollment. AFIS (Automated Fingerprint Identification System) is used for deduplication. First country in SADC to introduce AFIS. The upcoming system will be a multi-biometric platform.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Botswana's Omang (National Identity Card) system has been fully deployed nationwide since 1988, with a digital backend (NIS), AFIS biometrics, and 37 registration offices plus 13 hospital centers. A new electronic/digital ID card is under development with pilot expected 2025-2026.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The National Identity Management System (NIS) is linked with the electoral system, Social Benefit Registration System (SOBERS), government payroll, and transport system. Real-time updates occur when death registration events happen. The CRVS and NIS are mutually interoperable.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Bank of Botswana Banking Regulations require banks to demand Omang from citizens for opening accounts and conducting transactions. Regulation 5(1)(a) states banks 'shall require its personal customers...to produce...Omang identity card for a citizen of Botswana above the age of sixteen'. This is a mandatory requirement under law.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: First-time issuance of the Omang card is free. Renewal costs BWP5 (approximately US$0.37). Birth registration is also free. Late registration fees were waived from 2014 onwards for vulnerable populations. Only replacement for lost/stolen cards attracts a significant fee (BWP110/~US$8).

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Botswana and Namibia reached a bilateral agreement in February 2023 allowing citizens to use national ID cards for cross-border business and tourism travel (up to 30 days per stay, 90 days per year). A bilateral agreement with Zambia for smart national ID cross-border travel was announced in February 2026. Botswana is part of the SADC regional DPI/eKYC initiative across 16 countries. Cross-border recognition is partial/bilateral, not formally interoperable at the full SADC level.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: National Registration Act requires enrollment within 30 days of turning 16 years old. Citizens must obtain Omang at age 16. This age threshold (16) falls in the 10-17 years range. The unique ID number given at birth is the same number used for the Omang card at age 16.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: National Registration Act CAP 01:02 makes national registration compulsory for every citizen of Botswana within 30 days of turning 16 or acquiring citizenship. Failure to register within the prescribed period attracts a fine. Registration is mandatory for all eligible citizens.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The Ministry of Health adopted Omang as the unique identifier for all citizens seeking public health services. Non-citizens use passport numbers. This serves as the universal patient identifier across the public health sector. The Omang number is the primary key for patient data linkages in the public health information system.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Omang is for Botswana citizens only. Non-citizens are registered in a separate Immigration and Citizenship System (ICS) — permanent residents, work permit holders, and refugees have separate registration. A project is ongoing to link NIS and ICS for a comprehensive Population Register. Some non-nationals (with permanent residence) have access to a form of registration but not the Omang card itself.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: The World Bank ID4D Country Diagnostic (2018) constitutes a formal independent security and quality review of Botswana's identity management system. The Omang card has first and second-level security features (visual and machine-readable). AFIS ensures uniqueness. Government formally cites 'data security and integrity management' as a component of the NIS. No evidence of a separate external cybersecurity audit process.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: BOCRA mandated compulsory SIM card registration requiring national ID for all citizens. The March 2024 deadline for compliance resulted in 609,222 unregistered SIMs being suspended. Orange Botswana requires National ID for citizens as the only accepted document. This is a mandatory regulatory requirement under the CRA Act 2012.
